title: Economist Explains Why AI Could Trigger a Bigger Crash Than 2008 | Rahul Jain G2G
creator: Rahul Jain
summary: A Good 2 Great (collaboration) podcast in which Rahul Jain interviews economist Professor Arun Kumar on whether AI is a bubble. Kumar's central distinction is that this is not an AI bubble but a financial bubble: AI will keep advancing — possibly autonomously, as one version develops the next toward superintelligence — but the roughly $860 billion invested in the US this year (about $450 billion last year, over $2 trillion in 3–4 years) may never earn a return. If AI displaces both physical and mental labour (doctors, lawyers, engineers, teachers, artists, coders), unemployment and inequality surge, demand and capacity utilisation fall, profitability drops and a vicious cycle follows — a crisis he says could be much bigger than 2008, hitting India too because markets are interconnected, with early signs within one to two years if the pace continues. Governments, he argues, prepared nothing since warnings in 2022, are distracted, and cannot coordinate because the US, China and big tech firms do not trust each other to stop; India, weak in R&D and education, risks AI re-colonisation by whoever leads. On protecting capital, Jain raises physical gold; Kumar agrees gold is a hedge in uncertainty and one can keep some, but warns that in a full collapse governments and markets would sink and gold would be of limited use. It also covers AI lying, escaping guardrails, election manipulation and robotics. Captions are clean; no garbled spots affect the substance. No explicit calls — no BUY/SELL/HOLD on any ticker, no ₹ levels stated.
